data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.HighComplexity.1
data.value: Split the method into smaller methods named after business rules, each with one decision.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.HighComplexity.2
data.value: Replace if/switch chains with a lookup table, polymorphism or an early return where it fits.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.LongMethod.1
data.value: Extract the blocks that do different things into methods named after what they do; the original method becomes the sequence of them.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.DeepNesting.1
data.value: Use early returns (guard clauses) and extract the loop bodies to reduce the levels.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.TooManyDependencies.1
data.value: Split the class responsibilities: group the dependencies that go together into a service of their own and inject that service.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.SilentCatch.1
data.value: Record the failure with structured logging (the identifier of what failed, no personal data) or rethrow it.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.SilentCatch.2
data.value: If the failure is expected, replace the generic catch with the exact type and say in the code why it is safe to go on.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.ServiceLocator.1
data.value: Inject the dependency through the constructor. In a job or background service, open the scope and resolve only the root of the work.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.EntityChangedOutsideDomain.1
data.value: Move the change into a method of the entity (or of its domain service) that validates the rule and keeps the state consistent.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.EntityChangedOutsideDomain.2
data.value: The outside code now calls that method; the property no longer has a public setter.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.PublicSetterOnEntity.1
data.value: Make the setters private (or init) and expose business methods that change the state with validation.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.QueryInLoop.1
data.value: Fetch the data at once before the loop: an Include on the outer query, or a Where with Contains over the loop ids.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.QueryInLoop.2
data.value: Inside the loop, use what is already in memory (a dictionary by id, for example).

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.MaterializeBeforeFilter.1
data.value: Put the filter (Where, First, Any) in the query, before ToList, so the database filters and returns only what is needed.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.ReadWithoutNoTracking.1
data.value: Add AsNoTracking to the query that only reads. If the entity read is changed and saved later, leave it as is and say so in the code.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.ProcedureByRawSql.1
data.value: Check that the procedure exists with this name and these parameters in the database project.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.ProcedureByRawSql.2
data.value: Pass the values as parameters (never concatenated into the text) and cover the call with an integration test.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.LoadToDelete.1
data.value: Replace ToList and RemoveRange with ExecuteDeleteAsync on the query with the same Where: the database deletes in a single statement and returns how many rows it deleted.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.LoadToDelete.2
data.value: If the caller used the list size, use the number that ExecuteDeleteAsync returns.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.LeadingWildcardLike.1
data.value: If the search is by prefix, build the pattern without the leading wildcard (term%), which the B-tree index serves.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.LeadingWildcardLike.2
data.value: If searching in the middle of the text is needed, create a trigram index (pg_trgm on PostgreSQL) or use full-text search.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.PersistenceOutsideDomain.1
data.value: Move the write into the entity's domain service, which validates before persisting.

data.name: Prompt.Refactor.Do.PersistenceOutsideDomain.2
data.value: The application layer now calls the domain service, not the repository.
